mstts:express-as.prosody: Chapter 9: Building Bridges—Reaching Across Divides. Over the years, the school’s influence starts to reach way beyond its own campus. Imagine this—graduates heading back to their hometowns, carrying new skills, fresh attitudes, and a different way of looking at the world. Some become teachers, passing on what they’ve learned. Others open up businesses, and a handful even decide to run for public office. The ripple effect is real, but let’s be honest—so are the challenges. Picture a small town where a former student sets up a carpentry shop. At first, business is slow. Folks aren’t sure—they wonder if they can trust someone from “the school.” But you know what? The quality of the work starts to speak for itself. Customers come back. Word gets around. Before long, the shop isn’t just a place to buy furniture—it turns into a gathering spot. It becomes a symbol of what’s possible when people invest in themselves, and in each other. Meanwhile, somewhere else, a group of graduates starts a community garden. They invite everyone—Black, white, young, old. At first? People hesitate. Old prejudices, old habits—they’re tough to break. But as the garden grows, so does something else: a sense of shared purpose. Folks who barely exchanged words before now find themselves planting side by side, sharing stories and laughter while tending rows of tomatoes and beans. And here’s what really stands out: Real change doesn’t come from speeches or new laws. It happens through relationships. When people come together to work toward something bigger than themselves, those old barriers start to fall away. That’s the school’s greatest legacy—not just the skills it teaches, but the bridges it helps people build. Of course, there are setbacks. Not every project works out. Not every heart is changed overnight. But the work keeps going. One conversation at a time. One project. One act of kindness. If there’s one lesson here, it’s this: Progress is possible. But it takes patience, humility, and a real willingness to see the humanity in others.
